title: Plan: Setup Local Python venv and Read Existing VBA
body:
# Plan: Setup Local Python venv and Read Existing VBA

- Confidence: 90%
- Version: v1.0

## Documents

- Truth: /workspace/01_excel_dashboard/v5.5_40L_Project_Tracker.xlsm
- References: oletools/olevba documentation (https://github.com/decalage2/oletools)
- Targets:
  - /workspace/01_excel_dashboard/.venv/ (new virtual environment)
  - /workspace/01_excel_dashboard/.gitignore (updated)
  - /workspace/01_excel_dashboard/vba_dump.txt (new, VBA source code from file)
- Dependencies:
  - Python 3.14.4 (installed)
  - venv module (installed)
- Tests: None

## Goal

1. Create a local Python virtual environment (so installs stay in-project)
2. Install oletools inside it
3. Extract the VBA source code from the .xlsm file
4. Save the VBA dump to a text file for review
5. Update .gitignore so the venv and Python artifacts are not committed

## Change Items

### Change 1 - Create Python virtual environment

- Type: BASH (python3 -m venv)
- File: .venv/
- FROM: (does not exist)
- TO: A new Python virtual environment at `.venv/`
- Reason: User wants installs local to project, not global
- Status: DONE

### Change 2 - Install oletools inside venv

- Type: BASH (pip install)
- File: .venv/lib/...
- FROM: empty venv
- TO: oletools installed in venv
- Reason: Needed to read VBA code (user approved)
- Status: DONE

### Change 3 - Extract VBA code from .xlsm

- Type: BASH (olevba)
- File: vba_dump.txt
- FROM: vbaProject.bin (121KB binary, inside .xlsm)
- TO: vba_dump.txt (human-readable VBA source code, 747 lines)
- Reason: User wants to read existing VBA before deciding what to change
- Status: DONE

### Change 4 - Update .gitignore

- Type: EDIT
- File: .gitignore
- FROM:
  ```
  .IDE_Plans/
  ```
- TO:
  ```
  .IDE_Plans/
  .venv/
  __pycache__/
  *.pyc
  *.pyo
  vba_dump.txt
  ```
- Reason: User wants venv and Python artifacts ignored. Also ignoring the dump so we don't commit a generated file by accident.
- Status: DONE

## Notes

- vba_dump.txt is added to gitignore because it is a generated file. If the user wants to commit it later, they can use `git add -f`.
- All Python work happens inside `.venv/`. The system Python stays clean.
- We are NOT modifying the .xlsm file. Read-only.

## Retrospective

- What went well: venv created cleanly, oletools installed, olevba produced full dump, .gitignore hides all generated artifacts
- What failed: Nothing
- What to improve next time: Could split dump into per-module files for easier review next time
